name: Paranal Observatory and the Very Large Telescope
place: Cerro Paranal, Atacama Desert, Antofagasta Region
description: ESO's observatory on Cerro Paranal at 2,635 m, home of the Very Large Telescope: four 8.2 m telescopes that can also work together as an interferometer, plus four 1.8 m auxiliary telescopes. It also hosts the VISTA and VLT Survey Telescopes.
highlights: In 2004 the VLT took the first direct image of a planet outside the Solar System, 2M1207b.
The VLT tracked stars orbiting the supermassive black hole at the centre of the Milky Way, and in 2018 measured gravitational redshift there, a test of general relativity.
It observed the afterglow of GRB 090423, the most distant gamma-ray burst known at the time.
